pr_title: terraform test: Push evaluation of variables to as late as possible
pr_body:
<!--

Describe in detail the changes you are proposing, and the rationale.

See the contributing guide:

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md

-->

This PR pulls out the logic of evaluating variables for the terraform test framework into a shared variable cache. This cache can then be shared between the provider configurations and the run blocks. Within the testing framework we have to avoid evaluating variables until we know which run block they will be used in. This is because the `variable` block provides the type of the variable, and helps us to parse it properly. The `variable` blocks are only available via the configuration under test, and this is not available until the run blocks are executing.

Previously, we were evaluating all the file level variables once at the beginning of the test execution. This led to variables that were required by the modules other than the main configuration being misconfigured due to missing `variable` blocks. Now, we delay evaluating the file level variables until they are needed via the cache. The cache ensures that we don't evaluate the same variable twice when processing provider configurations and run block variables as they happen separately.

A follow up PR to this will be introduced in time for v1.9, which will allow variable blocks to be defined within the test file itself. This will allow users to specify the type of file level and global variables without needing to tie them to a specific run block.

<!--

Link all GitHub issues fixed by this PR, and add references to prior
related PRs.

-->

Fixes #35005

issue_context.title: terraform test command does not honor TF_VAR_* environment variables when "module" is specified after 1.8.0
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version

```shell
Terraform v1.8.0
on linux_amd64
```


### Terraform Configuration Files

a dummy module, with a test, and a module used by the test:

main.tf:
```hcl
resource null_resource foo {}
```

foo/main.tf:
```hcl
variable "foo" {}
output "foo" {
    value = var.foo
}
```

foo.tftest.hcl:
```hcl
run "foo" {
    module {
        source = "./foo"
    }
}
```


### Debug Output

cannot post publicly.

### Expected Behavior

```bash
$ TF_VAR_foo=something terraform test
foo.tftest.hcl... in progress
  run "foo"... pass
foo.tftest.hcl... tearing down
foo.tftest.hcl... pass

Success! 1 passed, 0 failed.
```

### Actual Behavior

```bash
$ TF_VAR_foo=something terraform test
foo.tftest.hcl... in progress
  run "foo"... fail
╷
│ Error: Required variable not set
│ 
│   on foo/main.tf line 1:
│    1: variable "foo" {}
│ 
│ The variable "foo" is required, but is not set.
╵
foo.tftest.hcl... tearing down
foo.tftest.hcl... fail
Failure! 0 passed, 1 failed.
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```bash
TF_VAR_foo=something terraform test
```

### Additional Context

this does not happen on 1.7.x terraform versions. This also only seems to happen for tests with a custom module, ie:
```hcl
run {
  module {
    source = "./a-custom-module"
  }
}
```

### References

_No response_
comments: This appears to be an issue with the parsing behavior for environment variables and variables passed via command line for this specific scenario. I noticed that bools and integers still seem to work, but strings fail. Wrapping the string value with quotes gets rid of the error, but that's definitely not in line with normal parsing behavior.

Thanks @bminahan73, I can replicate this so I've marked it as confirmed.

It seems that we're not connecting the global variables (ie. environment variables, command line variables or variable file variables) up to the types defined within the alternate modules correctly. This means that Terraform doesn't know the correct type for your variable, and it is silently swallowing that error.

There's two errors in there. Firstly, it's not working out the type when it should, and secondly, it's not reporting the type error and simply stating the variable isn't defined when it is.

As pointed out by @mjgoethe, you can force the correct type by surrounding the input value in quotation marks which forces the type into a string and allows Terraform to parse it properly. This might work for you as a short-term workaround.

I will try and have a fix in place for this in time for v1.8.1. Thanks again for filing this.
Thank you for the fast fix!
Yes, please see the release notes: https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/v1.8/CHANGELOG.md#182-april-24-2024

If you have found a problem that seems similar to this, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.
